title: 第153章 立春第152章 冬藏
content_zh:
立春那天，青州城的雪开始化了。屋檐下的冰棱滴着水，滴在青石板上，砸出一个个浅坑。方圆站在院子里，看着墙角的枣树。枝条上那些芽比冬天的时候鼓了一些，透着淡淡的青色。他伸手碰了一下，没有缩回来，就那么放了一会儿。王紫璇来的时候，看到他在摸树芽，“立春了？”“嗯。”“那今年会比去年暖和。”“不一定。”王紫璇没有反驳，把带来的菜放进厨房，又走出来，在石凳上坐下。
中午的时候，太阳照在身上有了一点暖意。方圆把厚棉袄脱了，搭在椅背上，穿着一件薄衫在院子里走了一圈。王紫璇坐在石凳上，看着他走。“你觉得今年会是什么样？”“不知道。但会比去年好。”王紫璇没有问他为什么这么说，只是坐着，看他走完那几圈，然后站起来，“走吧，去买树苗。城东老孙头的苗圃开市了。”“买什么树苗？”“去了再看。”
两人沿着街道往城东走。路面的雪已经化了大半，露出湿漉漉的青石板。街上有几个小孩在跑，踩着水洼，溅起一片片水花。城东的苗圃在一条巷子的尽头，门口摆着几捆树苗，还沾着湿润的土。方圆蹲下来看了一圈，挑了一棵桃树苗，树干细瘦，枝上的芽苞已经透出淡淡的粉意。他回头看了一眼王紫璇，她正站在旁边看一棵枇杷树苗。“桃树种在靠墙的地方，春天开花，秋天不一定能结果。”“那就先看花。”方圆付了钱，把桃树苗夹在腋下，起身往回走。王紫璇跟在他身后，走得不快。阳光照在他们背上，两个人的影子一前一后，像是春天的第一批脚印。
回到院子，方圆在墙角选了一个位置，在枣树和杏树之间挖了一个坑，把桃树苗放进去，填土，拍实，浇了水。王紫璇站在他身后，“三棵树了。”“嗯。”“过几年，春天会很好看。”方圆把水瓢放下，看了看那三棵树，又看了看王紫璇，觉得春天确实快来了。
第二天，方小石来了。他站在门口，看着墙角那棵新种的桃树，“方圆哥，你又种了一棵树？”“嗯。”“这棵会结果吗？”“会。但要等两年。”方小石点了点头，在桃树前面蹲了下来，又站起来，“方圆哥，等我长大了，你还会住在这里吗？”“会。”“那我就还能看到这棵树结果。”方圆没有说话。方小石在院子里待了一会儿，看了看桃树，又看了看枣树和杏树，然后转身走了。他走得不快，像是已经把某个答案留在了这座院子里。
方圆站在院子里，看着方小石的身影在巷子口消失，又转身看向那棵新种下的桃树。它还很细，枝条不多，但每一根都是直的，已经开始为这个春天做准备了。他走到井边，又打了一桶水，给三棵树都浇了一遍。
又过了几天，天气更暖了一些。青州城的雪化得差不多了，屋檐下不再滴水，墙角那几棵树开始长出更明显的芽。方圆早晨起来去院子里浇水，发现桃树的枝条上冒出了几粒粉色的花苞。很小，藏在叶子中间，像是刚刚醒过来的眼睛。他蹲下来看了一会儿，站起来，走进厨房。王紫璇今天没有来。他生火，煮了一锅粥，喝了两碗，把剩下的留给她。傍晚的时候，院门被推开了。王紫璇站在门口，手里拎着一条鱼。“来晚了。”“鱼哪来的？”“东市买的。今天有渔船回来，我买了一条。”她走进厨房，把鱼放在案板上。方圆跟进去，站在她身后，“今天怎么这么晚？”“去了一趟城外。看了看河。冰已经化了，水在流。”她说着，开始刮鱼鳞，动作利落，像是早就知道春天会从哪条河流先来。方圆站在她身后看了一会儿，然后退出厨房，走到院子里。夕阳的光斜斜地照在墙角的桃树上，那几粒花苞在光里微微发亮。
晚饭的时候，鱼炖好了。白嫩的鱼肉躺在汤汁里，浮着几片姜和一撮葱花，香气从厨房一直飘到院子里。王紫璇把鱼端到石桌上，又盛了两碗饭，把筷子摆好。方圆在她对面坐下，夹起一块鱼肉，尝了尝——很鲜，肉质紧实，带着葱姜的香气。“好吃。”他说。“吃吧。”王紫璇也夹了一块，嚼得很慢，像是要把整个春天都嚼碎了咽下去。
天快黑的时候，王紫璇站起来，“我回去了。”方圆也站起来，“我送你。”两人走到巷子口，王紫璇停下来，“不用送了。院子里的树刚浇过水，你回去看看，别让土被晚风吹松了。”方圆站在巷子口，看着她走进暮色里。她走得比平时慢，像是也在等春天一步步落稳。他转身走回院子，蹲下来，摸了摸桃树根部的土——还是湿的。风从墙外吹过来，带着泥土解冻后特有的气息。他站起来，走进屋里，没有点灯，在黑暗中坐了一会儿，听着远处隐约的水声，觉得万物都在慢慢醒来。
第二天早上，方圆推开院门，发现门口放着一把野花。花是黄色的，小小的，像是刚从田埂上摘下来的，还带着清晨的露水。他蹲下来看了一会儿，没有捡起来，就那么让它放在门口。过了一会儿，王紫璇来了。她走到门口，低头看了一眼那把野花，像是早就知道它会出现在那里。她弯腰捡起来，拿在手里，走进院子，把花插在石桌上的一个粗陶瓶里。那是她上次带来的瓶子，空了好一阵子。方圆站在正房门口看着她插花，动作不算熟练，像是很久没有做过这件事了，但最终还是把花拢出了一个合适的形状。她直起身，退后半步看了看，又伸手扶了扶其中一朵歪斜的花。“好看。”方圆说了一句。王紫璇没有回头，但她的声音里带着一丝舒展的笑意：“那当然。”方圆看着她，又看了看墙角那三棵树，觉得院子突然亮堂了许多。桃树上的花苞比昨天更鼓了，像是已经认定了春天，在等一个不慌不忙的日子，一起开。
傍晚，方圆把石桌上的粗陶瓶端进屋里，放在窗台上。窗台上那些东西——干枣、信、杏核、李子核——都还在，现在多了一把野花。他看了一会儿，又把它端回石桌上，让风也能吹到它。然后他坐下，等着天黑，等着明天，等着那些花苞一张一张地把春天打开。
：8xiaoshuo。：wap.8xiaoshuo
content_en:
On the day of the beginning of spring, the snow in Qingzhou City began to melt. The icy edges under the eaves were dripping with water, dripping onto the bluestone slabs and creating shallow pits. Fangyuan stood in the yard, looking at the jujube tree in the corner. The buds on the branches are more bulging than in winter, showing a light green color. He reached out and touched it, but didn't pull it back. He just left it there for a while. When Wang Zixuan came, she saw him touching the tree buds, "Is it the beginning of spring?" "Yeah." "Then this year will be warmer than last year." "Not necessarily." Wang Zixuan did not refute, put the vegetables he brought into the kitchen, walked out, and sat down on the stone bench.
At noon, the sun shone a little warmly on my body. Fangyuan took off his thick cotton-padded jacket, put it on the back of the chair, and walked around the yard wearing a thin shirt. Wang Zixuan sat on the stone bench and watched him go. "What do you think it will be like this year?" "I don't know. But it will be better than last year." Wang Zixuan didn't ask him why he said that. She just sat and watched him finish the few laps, then stood up and said, "Let's go buy saplings. The nursery in Laosuntou in the east of the city is open." "What saplings to buy?" "We'll see after we get there."
The two of them walked along the street to the east of the city. Most of the snow on the road has melted, revealing wet bluestone. There were several children running on the street, stepping on puddles and splashing water. The nursery in the east of the city is at the end of an alley. There are several bundles of saplings at the door, still covered with moist soil. Fangyuan knelt down and looked around, and picked out a peach sapling. The trunk was thin and the buds on the branches were already showing a faint pink color. He looked back at Wang Zixuan, who was standing next to a loquat sapling. "The peach tree is planted against the wall. It blooms in spring but may not bear fruit in autumn." "Then let's see the flowers first." Fangyuan paid the money, held the peach sapling under his arm, stood up and walked back. Wang Zixuan followed him, not walking fast. The sun shone on their backs, and their shadows moved one behind the other, like the first footprints of spring.
Back in the yard, Fangyuan chose a spot in the corner, dug a hole between the jujube and apricot trees, put the peach saplings in, filled it with soil, patted it down, and watered it. Wang Zixuan stood behind him, "Three trees." "Yeah." "In a few years, spring will be beautiful." Fangyuan put down the water ladle, looked at the three trees, and then at Wang Zixuan, feeling that spring was indeed coming soon.
The next day, Fang Xiaoshi came. He stood at the door and looked at the newly planted peach tree in the corner, "Brother Fangyuan, have you planted another tree?" "Yes." "Will this tree bear fruit?" "Yes. But it will take two years." Fang Xiaoshi nodded, squatted down in front of the peach tree, and stood up again, "Brother Fangyuan, when I grow up, will you still live here?" "Yes." "Then I can still see this tree bear fruit." Fangyuan said nothing. Fang Xiaoshi stayed in the yard for a while, looked at the peach trees, then at the jujube and apricot trees, then turned and left. He walked slowly, as if he had left some answer in this courtyard.
Fangyuan stood in the yard, watching Fang Xiaoshi's figure disappear at the entrance of the alley, then turned to look at the newly planted peach tree. It is still very thin, with not many branches, but each one is straight, and it has begun to prepare for this spring. He walked to the well, fetched another bucket of water, and watered all three trees.
A few days later, the weather got warmer. The snow in Qingzhou City has almost melted, water is no longer dripping under the eaves, and the trees in the corners have begun to grow more obvious buds. Fangyuan got up in the morning and went to water the yard, and found a few pink buds sprouting from the branches of the peach tree. Very small, hidden among the leaves, like eyes that have just woken up. He knelt down and watched for a while, then stood up and walked into the kitchen. Wang Zixuan did not come today. He lit a fire, cooked a pot of porridge, drank two bowls, and left the rest to her. In the evening, the courtyard door was pushed open. Wang Zixuan stood at the door, holding a fish in her hand. "It's late." "Where did the fish come from?" "I bought it from Dongshi. Today.A fishing boat came back and I bought one. She walked into the kitchen and put the fish on the chopping board. Fangyuan followed her in and stood behind her, "Why is it so late today?" "Went for a trip outside the city." Looked at the river. The ice has melted and the water is flowing. "As she spoke, she began to scrape the fish scales, with neat movements, as if she already knew which river spring would come from first. Fangyuan stood behind her and watched for a while, then exited the kitchen and walked to the yard. The light of the setting sun slanted on the peach tree in the corner, and the few flower buds shone slightly in the light.
By dinner time, the fish was stewed. The white and tender fish meat lies in the soup, with a few slices of ginger and a pinch of chopped green onion floating on it. The aroma wafts from the kitchen to the yard. Wang Zixuan brought the fish to the stone table, filled it with two bowls of rice, and arranged the chopsticks. Fang Yuan sat down opposite her, picked up a piece of fish, and tasted it - it was very fresh, the meat was firm, with the aroma of onions and ginger. “Delicious. "He said. "Eat. "Wang Zixuan also took a piece and chewed it very slowly, as if she wanted to chew up the entire spring and swallow it.
When it was getting dark, Wang Zixuan stood up and said, "I'm going back. "Fang Yuan also stood up, "I'll give it to you. "When the two of them reached the entrance of the alley, Wang Zixuan stopped and said, "No need to send it off. The trees in the yard have just been watered. Go back and take a look to make sure the soil doesn't get loosened by the evening wind. "Fang Yuan stood at the entrance of the alley, watching her walk into the dusk. She walked slower than usual, as if she was also waiting for spring to settle down step by step. He turned and walked back to the yard, squatted down, and touched the soil at the base of the peach tree - it was still wet. The wind blew from outside the wall, carrying the unique smell of thawed soil. He stood up, walked into the house, without lighting, and sat in the darkness for a while, listening to the faint sound of water in the distance, feeling that everything was slowly waking up.
The next morning, Fangyuan opened the courtyard door and found a handful of wild flowers at the door. The flowers are yellow and small, as if they had just been picked from the field ridge, still carrying the morning dew. He knelt down and looked at it for a while, but didn't pick it up and just left it at the door. After a while, Wang Zixuan came. She walked to the door and glanced down at the handful of wild flowers, as if she had known it would appear there. She bent down to pick it up, held it in her hand, walked into the yard, and put the flowers in a stoneware vase on the stone table. That was the bottle she brought last time, it had been empty for a while. Fangyuan stood at the door of the main room and watched her arrange flowers. Her movements were not very skillful, as if she hadn't done this for a long time, but she finally managed to get the flowers into a suitable shape. She straightened up, took a half step back to take a look, and then stretched out her hand to support one of the crooked flowers. "Good looking. "Fang Yuan said. Wang Zixuan did not look back, but there was a hint of relaxed smile in her voice: "Of course. "Fang Yuan looked at her, then at the three trees in the corner, and felt that the yard suddenly became much brighter. The buds on the peach trees were more swollen than yesterday, as if they had recognized spring and were waiting for a calm day to bloom together.
In the evening, Fangyuan brought the stoneware bottle on the stone table into the house and placed it on the windowsill. The items on the windowsill—dried dates, letters, apricot pits, and plum pits—are all still there, but now there are a handful of wild flowers. He looked at it for a while and then brought it back to the stone table so that the wind could blow it. Then he sat down, waiting for dark, waiting for tomorrow, waiting for those buds to open up spring one by one.
